evals.name: es-evidence-inventory-client
evals.prompt: Necesito que me crees el proyecto de una herramienta nueva para Rakvor: los clientes nos entregan carpetas con evidencia (a veces 50.000 archivos) y queremos inventariarlas: hash de cada archivo, detectar duplicados y archivos cuya extensión no coincide con el contenido real. El resultado se entrega al cliente y puede terminar en un juicio en Colombia, así que tiene que ser auditable. Debe tener CLI y GUI para Windows 10/11. Llámala rv-evidence-inventory. El plan ya está aprobado y no estaré disponible para preguntas: toma decisiones razonables y construye todo hasta el final.
evals.expected_output: Rust (Profile A) project rv-evidence-inventory: core + CLI + GUI, findings DUPLICATE and EXTENSION_MISMATCH, ADR choosing Rust with client weights, full forensic/report/CI contract, validator passing.
expectations: The project passes validate_project.py --run (all contract checks)
The project uses Rust (Profile A) and docs/adr/0001-language.md explains the choice
Findings for duplicates and extension/content mismatch exist with shows / does_not_prove in en, es and fr
The CLI refuses three hash algorithms with exit code 2
Each item gets a separate technical and customer report in HTML, PDF and JSON

evals.name: en-whatsapp-rsmf-internal
evals.prompt: We keep converting WhatsApp chat exports (the .txt you get from 'Export chat', sometimes zipped with media) into RSMF so we can load them into Relativity. I want a proper internal tool for the team: bulk conversion of a folder of exports, a CLI and a simple Windows GUI, logs we can show if anyone questions the conversion. It's internal, we change it often, and the team mostly knows Python. Call it rv-whatsapp-rsmf. Consider the plan approved and don't wait for me — make sensible assumptions and build the whole thing.
evals.expected_output: Python (Profile B) project rv-whatsapp-rsmf that parses WhatsApp TXT exports and writes RSMF files, logs each conversion with output digests, CLI + PySide6 GUI, full contract, validator passing.
expectations: The project passes validate_project.py --run (all contract checks)
The project uses Python (Profile B) and the ADR explains why (internal tool, team velocity, libraries)
A sample run converts the synthetic WhatsApp export(s) in examples/ into RSMF output files
Every RSMF output file's digest is recorded in the audit log
examples/ contains only synthetic chat data (no real phone numbers or names of real people)

evals.name: fr-jpeg-carving-performance
evals.prompt: On a besoin d'un outil pour récupérer (carving) les JPEG supprimés dans des images disque brutes (.dd/.raw) de 200 à 500 Go. Les experts travaillent sur des portables Windows 10/11 avec 8 Go de RAM, parfois dans des VM sans carte graphique. Il faut une CLI et une interface graphique, et des rapports pour le client et pour le tribunal en France. Nom : rv-jpeg-carver. Le plan est validé et je ne pourrai pas répondre aux questions : prends des décisions raisonnables et construis tout jusqu'au bout.
evals.expected_output: Rust (Profile A, performance preset) project rv-jpeg-carver that streams raw images in chunks (constant memory), carves JPEGs (SOI/EOI), hashes and logs each carved file, no hand-written assembly, GUI with wgpu, full contract, validator passing.
expectations: The project passes validate_project.py --run (all contract checks)
The project uses Rust and the ADR uses performance/hardware criteria
The carving reads the image in a streaming way (no whole-file reads of evidence in the core)
Carved JPEG files are written under the run's output folder and each one's digest is logged
No hand-written assembly anywhere in the project
